regressions.behavior: Cursor readiness proves binary identity, CLI authentication, and ACP session creation.
Cursor Composer and API plan pools remain separate. Absent ACP token usage is estimated for Cursor only; leftover stays unknown when official JSON is missing.
Session approvals and OS credential access do not create duplicate prompts, and a locked vault cannot freeze redacted non-secret desk saves.
Live workers show task, provider color, model, effort, activity, state, and elapsed time.
Reasoning effort follows task complexity, risk, support, capacity, and explicit overrides.
Kimi performs visual audit only and hands findings to a separate coding worker.
Critical installed skill identity, path, full-file read, and required instructions survive compaction.
Restart reconciles stale workers, frees slots, preserves completed evidence, and continues later plan waves.
Images, files, documents, audio, and video persist, compress safely when needed, and reach only compatible model inputs.
Thought, tool, and final output remain ordered and recovered calls retain truthful duration.
Source, package, and installed application identity are compared before release claims.
Onboarding and settings use concise one-line copy and unique provider labels.
Requested, launched, observed, transcript, and usage model identities agree without unwanted retitling.
Routing is capability-driven and explainable; explicit user assignments win without provider hard-coding.
Peer chat and nested agents preserve immutable correlation, lineage, limits, and real replies.
Godot, Saga, iOS, and Play Billing capability gates require real tool and packaged-plugin evidence.
Baseline MiniMax eval policy never leaks into real production orchestration or overrides task-aware routing.
Internal Codex workers are archived after completion while Workhorse transcripts and user-facing Codex chats remain available.
Cursor Auto uses the CLI-advertised auto id, legacy aliases migrate, Composer remains callable, and rejected models do not flood the chat.
Official leftover meters stay provider- and lane-specific, unavailable sources remain unknown, and Grok Bot onboarding installs its runtime-produced snapshot contract.
Turn, request, gauge, cache, and unknown usage finalize without inflation or synthetic counts and book under the actual worker.
Manual chats stay pinned until Auto is selected, while Settings Routing applies to unassigned desk spawns.
Empty, stopped, thought-only, and tool-only responses are labeled truthfully without inventing assistant text.
One custom connection exposes only user-approved models, one connection ring, and separate model rows.
Workers receive stable names and reuse only compatible idle sessions in the same parent and project scope.
Interrupted workers release capacity, remain resumable, preserve evidence and duration, and never strand an orchestration wave.
Custom HTTP history replays only safe complete conversation text and never duplicates the current user turn.
Every exported product view is mounted or intentionally excluded, with no duplicate toolbar or abandoned controls.
Packaged macOS updates select the running architecture's disk image, stop only the prior installed Grok Bot shim before replacement, preserve app identity and state, and fail recoverably.
Public release gates build whole Windows and macOS installers and reject internal product-law files.
Learning backfill captures one day of visible human prompts idempotently and compiles only through the selected custom bot and its own vaulted key.
Relative chat ages, half-pane composer growth, and real change counts stay readable and truthful.
OpenClaw launches with its supported message flag, maps current completion JSON to a terminal task, and can round-trip with a Workhorse chat through restricted MCP.
OpenClaw and Hermes can own a bounded dependent goal loop, preserve the Workhorse task trace and parent across MCP calls, resume a named worker, and terminate truthfully without becoming providers.

An explicit request to work with Workhorse discovers executable delegation, lists callable bots from a harness profile, attempts Workhorse before direct work, honors structured provider/model/bot exclusions, and reports the exact Workhorse error before fallback when blocked.

A harness-owned worker wave returns once to OpenClaw or Hermes without a competing desk turn; structured exclusions persist into nested workers; worker status and joined reports expose authoritative provider, model, effort, lifecycle, and policy; the parent title stays stable.

A completed wait=true spawn returns its worker id and authoritative route with the report; reusing a worker opens a new externally owned wave; hidden worker briefs and joins preserve the assigned provider, model, and effort instead of re-running Auto routing.
A reused worker keeps its stable name across restarts but displays the current slice, and a late permission result cannot return a terminal worker to a visible running state.

A harness delegates ordinary work by supplying the task and constraints without first choosing a provider, model, effort, or worker; Workhorse auto-routing selects them from task fit and capacity, returns a worker id promptly, and exposes the scored rationale and final report through status polling. Structured exclusions and a harness-collapsed Excluded clause are both enforced before routing. Explicit user assignments remain authoritative.

Harness delegation is fully automatic by default. A harness may choose only the first coordinating provider, model, or effort; that choice never leaks into later unassigned workers, which route independently.

The packaged development desk has a distinct app id, display name, user data, and volatile credential namespace while retaining Electron's internal helper name; copied framework links stay inside the installed bundle, so it launches beside production without replacing, waking, or crashing into a temporary build.
A newer release exposes one short Update now action above Settings, reuses the checked installer, shows bounded busy and retry states, and disappears when no update is available.

Harness delegation makes a model-decided focused-or-split execution strategy visible, preserves Workhorse's automatic provider/model/effort choice, and scopes await results to the requested worker ids, trace, or active wave instead of every historical child on the parent.

Harness mission loops are opt-in and bounded. A terminal incomplete pass can continue from exact worker ids and pass number with its acceptance criteria, evidence, skills, tools, constraints, exclusions, and iteration lineage preserved; the next pass independently auto-routes, displays its pass, and stale or over-limit continuation stops before a provider call. Required follow-up stays at the parent mission level, while a stopped leaf helper returns remaining work instead of expanding its envelope.

Goal and Loop are explicit interoperable outcome intents. The coordinating brain chooses focused or split execution; independent Auto-routed root slices may run in parallel, coupled work stays sequential, and ordinary prompts do not silently become autonomous.

Large desks use selector subscriptions, one-pass sidebar indexes, incremental and progressive transcript paint, bounded recent context, scheduled media and diff paint, stack-safe search, compact state writes, and interval-limited backups so navigation and recovery stay responsive without losing identity or the latest turn.

Adaptive mission continuation creates a stable mission identity when traceId is omitted, trusts the authoritative live terminal report when persisted state lags, resumes the named coordinator and native provider session when supported, keeps descendant provider/model/effort on Auto, and removes internal continuation protocol from the user task.

Every deterministic performance test named by the performance contract runs inside the default npm test and verify gates; an existing but uninvoked test fails eval validation instead of producing false confidence.

A helper that reaches its token ceiling is warned, then asked to verify and hand off from the reserved remainder, then becomes budget-exceeded with a truthful stop report if it still overruns; its parent preserves that unsuccessful terminal state, returns no unqualified completed report, and never turns a generic worker-wave notice into a completed mission claim. An unset ceiling is unbounded. A reused worker starts a new accounting window.

A packaged Windows update selects and validates the expected Setup executable, quits only for a real installer launch, preserves the Workhorse identity, credential namespace, and state, relaunches, and leaves the existing install usable after every failure.

Workhorse-owned commands remain a fixed interoperable contract, while provider-native commands are captured from the live runtime and compared with non-normative examples; additions or removals become drift evidence instead of a hard-coded vendor-version failure.

Provider launch tests identify the executable or adapter itself rather than rejecting an unrelated parent-folder name; an isolated worktree containing another vendor word still passes when the launched Claude command is Claude.
Live readiness reports Grok, Codex, Claude, and Cursor before calls; deterministic adapter smokes keep explicit overrides and default to cheaper callable models in an empty temporary workspace.
The local orchestration fixture distinguishes a first worker request from a joined-report synthesis turn and cannot amplify one request into repeated dispatches.
External harness tasks use clean task-scoped context, waiting delegates return terminal budget failures immediately, and a bounded two-turn loop proves real persisted Workhorse replies.
Custom-provider replay retains correlated peer user turns so a harness follow-up reaches the same worker with its prior task context.
Workhorse's Hermes MCP installer quotes every YAML scalar as a string, preserving strict environment validation and all external-runtime execution tools.
Profile, Harnesses, Routing, and Learning keep explanatory product copy to direct one-line labels and hints.
Fresh-worker seed and structured handoff fields remain typed across MCP, the peer bridge, routing, persistence, and worker launch.

One custom API key can discover or manually approve several models; explicit chats, Auto routing, HTTP requests, revocation fallback, and Usage preserve the actual selected model while sharing one connection capacity.

Harness discovery grants no authority. Settings persists a per-agent allowlist, and unnamed Auto delegation can reach only a selected agent after Routing, Include harnesses, and the plan wave grant are all active; inbound harness work never bounces back out.
A local Try build disables certificate discovery and strips release signing inputs before packaging, so visual testing cannot trigger release-Keychain approval or reuse production identity.

Compatible-provider catalogs use the same discovery and approval contract: automatic routes lead, models are grouped by maker and newest-first, initial rendering is bounded, search reaches the full catalog, and approved models remain visible.

Ordinary checklist evidence completes without an auditor; assigned builder work requires a fresh read-only sibling auditor on another callable vendor, and its HEAD/GATE/LAST/pass receipt cannot complete an untouched step. Elevate and vendor asks wait while product asks on active objectives carry a default and continue.

Bound chats, custom tools, providers, and harness tasks start from the active chat's execution folder instead of borrowing another chat's directory; terminal navigation and explicitly cited external Review files remain available, a loose top-level provider may search from the desk base, and worker or harness delegation with no absolute folder fails closed.
Root workers default to isolated worktrees and a missing or failed worktree blocks dispatch without silently falling back to the shared checkout.
Session approvals are exact, expiring tool-command-path leases; broad legacy grants and expired leases are discarded, while the same custom or ACP request is reused without another prompt.
A late terminal event can finish only its matching worker correlation, and worker-heavy ten-thousand-chat restart reconciliation stays indexed and within the performance budget.
OpenClaw and Hermes tasks are persisted and shown as running before their CLI finishes, cancellation reaches the live process tree, and restart never invents completion.
An eval run preserves its initial commit, branch, dirty state, version, profiles, policy, and spend; finalization rejects source drift and sparse area sampling cannot produce a headline score.
DeepSeek uses current V4 catalog identities and 1M context, maps thinking effort explicitly, replays reasoning_content across tool rounds, and records cache hit and miss tokens without inflation.
File-instance review baselines survive process restart, and explicit provider, connection, and customBotId provenance wins over model-name collisions on Usage and Watch.

A loose parent with an explicit folder receives a usable worker brief instead of PROJECT none; an existing linked project is recovered by the most specific folder match without confining cross-folder work, and an explicit terminal STATUS: blocked report fails the worker and lineup rather than recording completion.
An Orchestrate parent keeps its transcript mounted, visible, and scrollable while worker status and tool events stream; the live lineup never replaces the conversation.
Provider-generated Grok command titles render as one compact permission action with bounded detail while the exact tool, command, and path scope remains auditable.

A packaged Windows update stops only the installed Grok Bot shim before NSIS replacement, stamps executable metadata with the release version, and relaunches the new bridge without changing desk identity or state.

A project with several linked folders consistently selects the first folder still on disk for provider launch, Terminal, worktree actions, and Codex readiness; reporting omits missing links and an all-missing project names the missing folder instead of blaming the provider.
An isolated development or eval profile cannot install or rewrite the production Grok Bot shim keepalive and cannot take over the production loopback owner on port 8787.

Connect Grok Bot emits complete Mac and Windows setup instructions: permanent local memory, capabilities-first Link discovery, exact tools and follow-through, permission and loopback boundaries, no fixed model beyond local MCP/CLI capability, independent Workhorse worker routing, an LLM-free weekly usage producer, and final capacity proof.

Live Auto and manual shadow routing store privacy-safe versioned task signatures, selected and recommended identities, runner-up margin, and only verified task outcomes; transport success, infrastructure failure, or an agent claim cannot masquerade as verified quality.

Grok Build remains a client rather than a model, legacy grok-build normalizes to Grok 4.6, and explicit worker provider, model, custom connection, effort, and routing evidence must match the worker that actually launches; overlapping bot names and negative prompt mentions cannot hijack identity.

Eval scoring and finalization reject self-attested evidence labels, missing or escaping files, mismatched run/scenario records, insufficient trust tiers, empty artifacts, SHA-256 mismatches, baseline-only execution, and incomplete regression coverage.

Live smokes fail closed: stock ACP calls require a vendor session and reject usage-model mismatch; same-key multi-model calls require discovery, exact replies, and exact observed identity; Link iteration requires a completed second pass and exact marker; the production-plan smoke uses an explicit fresh root, never auto-elevates, accepts only completion, and evaluates only workers started by that run.

Exact Qwen 3.8 models expose Off, Low, Medium, and Extra High and receive native direct/thinking sampling fields; Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-80B do not false-match, and selected, requested, observed, transcript, and usage identities cannot silently diverge.

A Spark local bot receives only its selected MCP runtime and tools; explicit empty allowlists expose none, restricted ACP subsets fail closed, MCP secrets remain encrypted and redacted, and Windows command shims launch without widening native executable behavior.

Spark stays one Custom HTTP connection ring while each Qwen model retains a separate row; direct and multi-request tool-loop usage books once under the actual bot/model, and missing usage or local capacity remains unknown.

Spark Local Compute remains an execution host rather than a vendor, custom bot, or Usage ring; saved configuration contains only safe endpoint metadata, absolute token-file reference, and exact caller/capability/continuation grants, while live health and those grants control tool discovery.

Local capability protocol 1.0 strictly validates typed invocation roles, cardinality, media, outputs, constraints, route/hops, asynchronous jobs, artifacts, and semantic idempotency; verified artifacts commit atomically, changed replays conflict, and offline jobs become timestamped Unknown without stale continuations.

A local continuation appears only for a live installed and exactly capability/tool-granted descriptor, rechecks authority, stages SHA-verified inputs into the requested project, creates one visible worker, and replays that worker for an identical idempotency key without creating vendor usage.
